The studio was called "Eternal Serenity," a name that felt increasingly ironic as Jim, a man whose idea of stretching was reaching for the remote, sat in the back row of the "Advanced Vinyasa Flow" class. He had meant to join "Gentle Yoga for Beginners," but the sign-up sheet had been smudged, and in his haste to find a parking spot, he had simply picked the first mat that looked unoccupied.

The instructor, a woman named Seraphina who looked like she was made entirely of willow branches and judgment, clapped her hands once. The sound was like a whip crack. "Welcome, seekers of truth," she whispered, her voice echoing off the bamboo walls. "Today, we explore the Bridge of Unity. We lift our hips, we open our hearts, and we release all tension."

Jim looked around. Everyone else was already in a perfect, inverted V-shape, their bodies taut and graceful. Jim, whose spine was roughly shaped like a question mark, decided to mimic the person in front of him. He placed his hands on the mat, kicked his legs up, and attempted to lift his hips.

The problem was twofold. First, Jim had not warmed up. Second, Jim had eaten a large burrito for lunch.

As he strained to lift his glutes off the ground, his body did not form a bridge. It formed a tent. A very unstable, trembling tent. His face turned a shade of purple usually reserved for bruised plums. He grunted, a low, guttural sound that started in his toes and ended in his ears.

"Deeper into the pose, Jim," Seraphina said, gliding past him. She didn't look at him; she looked *through* him, as if he were a piece of furniture that needed dusting.

"I'm trying!" Jim wheezed, his voice an octave higher than usual.

He shifted his weight to adjust his balance. This was a mistake. The shift compressed his abdomen with the force of a hydraulic press. A small, high-pitched squeak escaped him. It sounded like a mouse being stepped on.

The woman next to him, who was currently balancing on one hand in a complex arm variation, froze. Her eye twitched.
